analyst_view.overall: Second-placed Brighton (22 points, six wins in their last seven league games, all with clean sheets) visit 14th-placed Hull (11 points), who are eight league games without a win but are one of four sides still unbeaten at home in the first Premier League meeting between the clubs. Jakirovic says Belloumi and Nobel Mendy are fit after the break (one preview still lists them as doubts) and Crooks is back from his ban, while Targett, Matazo, Morita and Ansah are out and Hughes is a doubt, all as the numbers assume. Brighton have Struijk, Chema and Hadjam back and Gross (new contract, 300th appearance, the league's top chance creator) in midfield; Minteh and Azeez face late fitness tests, and Mitoma, Ferguson, Yohanna and Tzimas are out and already counted. Expect Hull in a compact back five with about a third of the ball, playing direct to McBurnie, against Brighton's patient possession. Referee Peter Bankes (4.0 cards a game over 50 games, the league average) is counted, and with the morning team news matching what the numbers assumed I keep every stat where they put it.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals (Hull 1.1, Brighton 1.4), already trimming Hull a little for scoring only 6 in their last six. Brighton's run of clean sheets and Hull's narrow defeats and home draws point to a tight game, but that form is in the ratings, and Mitoma, Ferguson and Tzimas being out is already taken off Brighton; with Belloumi, Hull's main outlet, fit as assumed, I stay at 2.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners, already adding a little for Hull's recent rise (31 corners in six). Brighton average about 5 corners a game and Hull about 4, close to what the numbers show; Minteh is only a possible substitute and Mitoma is out, as assumed, and Hull's back five is their usual shape, so I stay at 9.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards, already counting Brighton's busier recent card count (16 in six) and referee Peter Bankes at 4.0 a game in his record. He has shown a few more yellows this season in a small sample, and Crooks (five bookings in ten) returns to battle Gross in midfield, but nothing points to a heated game beyond what the numbers see, so I stay at 3.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.0 shots, already adding about 8% to Brighton for their high recent output (102 shots in six). Season averages have Brighton at about 17 shots a game and Hull at about 10, the fewest in the league, which is what the ratings show, and Brighton's line-up is at normal strength, so I keep 27.0.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target, already lowering Hull's for poor recent accuracy (16 on target in six). Belloumi, Hull's main creator, is fit as the numbers assumed, and Brighton's attack around Gross, De Cuyper and Kostoulas is as expected without Mitoma, so I stay at 8.3.
